source_text: Ἔτι οὖν καὶ περὶ τοῦ σαββάτου γέγραπται ἐν τοῖς δέκα λόγοις, ἐν οἷς ἐλάλησεν ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ πρὸς Μωϋσῆν κατὰ πρόσωπον: Καὶ ἁγιάσατε τὸ σάββατον κυρίου χερσὶν καθαραῖς καὶ καρδίᾳ καθαρᾷ. καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει: Ἐὰν φυλάξωσιν οἱ υἱοί μου τὸ σάββατον, τότε ἐπιθήσω τὸ ἔλεός μου ἐπ’ αὐτούς. τὸ σάββατον λέγει ἐν ἀρχῇ τῆς κτίσεως: Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν ἓξ ἡμέραις τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνετέλεσεν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ καὶ κατέπαυσεν ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ ἡγίασεν αὐτήν. προσέχετε, τέκνα, τί λέγει τὸ συνετέλεσεν ἐν ἓξ ἡμέραις. τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι ἐν ἑξακισχιλίοις ἔτεσιν συντελέσει κύριος τὰ σύμπαντα: ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα παῤ αὐτῷ σημαίνει χίλια ἔτη. αὐτὸς δέ μοι μαρτυρεῖ λέγων: Ἰδού, ἡμέρα κυρίου ἔσται ὡς χίλια ἔτη. οὐκοῦν, τέκνα, ἐν ἓξ ἡμέραις, ἐν τοῖς ἑξακισχιλίοις ἔτεσιν συντελεσθήσεται τὰ σύμπαντα. Καὶ κατέπαυσεν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ. τοῦτο λέγει: ὅταν ἐλθὼν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ καταργήσει τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ ἀνόμου καὶ κρινεῖ τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς καὶ ἀλλάξει τὸν ἥλιον καὶ τὴν σελήνην καὶ τοὺς ἀστέρας, τότε καλῶς καταπαύσεται ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει: Ἁγιάσεις αὐτὴν χερσὶν καθαραῖς καὶ καρδίᾳ καθαρᾷ. εἰ οὖν ἣν ὁ θεὸς ἡμέραν ἡγίασεν νῦν τις δύναται ἁγιάσαι καθαρὸς ὢν τῇ καρδίᾳ, ἐν πᾶσιν πεπλανήμεθα. ἴδε ὅτι ἄρα τότε καλῶς καταπαυόμενοι ἁγιάσομεν αὐτήν, ὅτε δυνησόμεθα αὐτοὶ δικαιωθέντες καὶ ἀπολαβόντες τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν, μηκέτι οὔσης τῆς ἀνομίας, καινῶν δὲ γεγονότων πάντων ὑπὸ κυρίου: τότε δυνησόμεθα αὐτὴν ἁγιάσαι, αὐτοὶ ἁγιασθέντες πρῶτον. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει αὐτοῖς: Τὰς νεομηνίας ὑμῶν καὶ τὰ σάββατα οὐκ ἀνέχομαι. ὁρᾶτε, πῶς λέγει; οὐ τὰ νῦν σάββατα ἐμοὶ δεκτά, ἀλλὰ ὃ πεποίηκα, ἐν ᾧ καταπαύσας τὰ πάντα ἀρχὴν ἡμέρας ὀγδόης ποιήσω, ὅ ἐστιν ἄλλου κόσμου ἀρχήν. διὸ καὶ ἄγομεν τὴν ἡμέραν τὴν ὀγδόην εἰς εὐφροσύνην, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνέστη ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ φανερωθεὶς ἀνέβη εἰς οὐρανούς.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, it is also written concerning the Sabbath in the ten words, in which God spoke on Mount Sinai to Moses face to face: And you shall sanctify the Sabbath of the Lord with clean hands and a clean heart. And in another place it says: If my sons keep the Sabbath, then I will put my mercy on them. The Sabbath says at the beginning of creation: And God made the works of his hands in six days, and he finished on the seventh day and rested on it and sanctified it. Take heed, children, what it says, he finished in six days. This means that in six thousand years the Lord will finish all things, for the day with him signifies a thousand years. He himself bears witness to me, saying: Behold, the day of the Lord will be as a thousand years. Therefore, children, in six days, in the six thousand years, all things will be finished. And he rested on the seventh day. This means: when the Son comes and destroys the time of the lawless one and judges the ungodly and changes the sun and the moon and the stars, then he will rightly rest on the seventh day. For it says: You shall sanctify it with clean hands and a clean heart. If then someone can sanctify the day which God sanctified, now being clean in heart, we have all gone astray. See that then, resting well, we will sanctify it, when we ourselves, having been justified and having received the promise, with no more lawlessness, and all things having been made new by the Lord, then we will be able to sanctify it, having been sanctified ourselves first. For it says to them: Your new moons and Sabbaths I do not endure. See how it says: not the present Sabbaths are acceptable to me, but what I have made, in which, having rested, I will make the beginning of the eighth day, which is the beginning of another world. Therefore, we also celebrate the eighth day with joy, on which Jesus also rose from the dead and, having appeared, ascended into the heavens.

pass_b_english: It is also written about the Sabbath in the ten words which God spoke face to face with Moses on Mount Sinai: "You shall sanctify the Sabbath of the Lord with clean hands and a clean heart" (Exod 20:8–11). Elsewhere it says: "If my sons keep the Sabbath, then I will put my mercy upon them" (Exod 31:13). At the beginning of creation the Sabbath declares: "And God made the works of his hands in six days, and he finished on the seventh day and rested on it and sanctified it" (Exod 20:8–11). Children, pay attention to what "he finished in six days" means. It means that in six thousand years the Lord will finish all things, for with him a day signifies a thousand years. He himself testifies to me, saying, "Behold, the day of the Lord will be as a thousand years" (Ps 90:4). So then, children, in six days—that is, in six thousand years—all things will be finished. "And he rested on the seventh day." This means: when his Son comes and destroys the reign of the lawless one, judges the ungodly, and changes the sun, the moon, and the stars, then he will truly rest on the seventh day. For it says: "You shall sanctify it with clean hands and a clean heart." If anyone can now sanctify the day which God sanctified while being clean in heart, we have all gone astray. Understand, then, that we will sanctify it by resting properly only when we ourselves have been justified and have received the promise, when lawlessness is no more and all things have been made new by the Lord; then we will be able to sanctify it, having first been sanctified ourselves. For he says to them: "Your new moons and your Sabbaths I cannot endure" (Isa 1:13). See how he speaks: the present Sabbaths are not acceptable to me, but the one I have made, in which, after I have rested, I will make the beginning of the eighth day, which is the beginning of another world. That is why we also keep the eighth day with joy—the day on which Jesus rose from the dead, appeared, and ascended into the heavens.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the millennialist interpretation of the six days and the theological significance of the eighth day. Scripture citations in Pass B (Exod 20:8–11, Exod 31:13, Ps 90:4, Isa 1:13) correctly identify the biblical sources alluded to in the Greek text.
